title: Airlock: your first run
description: What actually happens when you type ai-start, in nine steps. Written for someone who has never run a local model before.

nodes.label: You
nodes.description: One command. You do not need to know which port, which model, or which backend.

nodes.label: ai-start
nodes.description: Start-AI.ps1 — the front door. Decides the backend, enforces single-instance, binds the port, guards the firewall.

nodes.label: provider-policy
nodes.description: Your saved intent: which backend you prefer, whether cloud fallback is allowed at all.

nodes.label: capability check
nodes.description: Get-BackendCapability.ps1 — is vLLM even possible here? Needs an NVIDIA GPU and Docker running.

nodes.label: model picker
nodes.description: Get-ModelAcquisition.ps1 — sizes candidate models against FREE VRAM, not system RAM (ADR-005), and pulls one if you have none.

nodes.label: Ollama
nodes.description: The local inference engine. One instance, always — never two competing for the same GPU.

nodes.label: firewall guard
nodes.description: Blocks inbound on the port. Defence in depth: the listener is loopback-only regardless.
One stable address. Every tool you point here keeps working when the model behind it changes.

nodes.label: audit log
nodes.description: Every state change, timestamped. This is also what Generate-LiveScene.ps1 turns back into a scene.

nodes.label: your AI tools
nodes.description: aider, Claude Code, opencode, Codex — all pointed at the same endpoint.

steps.caption: You type ai-start. That is the whole command.
steps.detail: No port to choose, no model name to memorise, no environment variables to export by hand.

steps.caption: Airlock reads what you asked for last time.
steps.detail: provider-policy.json holds your intent. It is deliberately separate from what is running right now, so a crashed session can never look like a changed preference.

steps.caption: It checks whether the faster backend is even possible on this machine.
steps.detail: vLLM needs an NVIDIA GPU and Docker running. If either is missing you are never offered it — no failed launch, no confusing error.

steps.caption: It picks a model that fits your graphics card.
steps.detail: Sized against free VRAM, not free system RAM. A model that spills onto the CPU technically runs, but each turn takes minutes — which for an interactive loop is the same as broken.

steps.caption: One backend starts. Exactly one, always.
steps.detail: Any stray instance from an earlier session is found and stopped first, so two copies never fight over the same GPU memory.

steps.caption: A firewall rule blocks the port from the outside.
steps.detail: Belt and braces — the listener is already bound to loopback only, so nothing off your machine could reach it either way.

steps.caption: You get one stable address: 127.0.0.1:12345.
steps.detail: Swap the model, swap the backend, and this address does not change. Nothing you configured yesterday breaks today.

steps.caption: Every step of that is written to an audit log.
steps.detail: Which model, which backend, when, and whether it succeeded. This scene can be regenerated from that log.

steps.caption: Now point any AI tool at it and start working.
steps.detail: For Claude Code, run ai-claude-on — it redirects this shell only, checks the port is alive first, and ai-claude-off puts it back.
